items.headline: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna into ChatGPT, Codex, and the API
items.diff_narrative: New today: OpenAI moved the GPT-5.6 family from limited preview to broad rollout on July 9, absent from yesterday's report. The launch lands a three-tier price ladder (Sol $5/$30, Terra $2.50/$15, Luna $1/$6 per million tokens), a max reasoning effort setting, and a subagent-driven ultra mode, with GitHub Copilot picking up all three tiers same-day. It directly reshapes the frontier-pricing landscape that yesterday's Grok 4.5 story ($2/$6) was competing in: Terra now matches GPT-5.5-class performance at roughly half its cost, resetting the mid-tier floor rivals price against.

items.headline: Meta starts charging for frontier AI with Muse Spark 1.1 and its first external Meta Model API
items.diff_narrative: New today: Meta Superintelligence Labs released Muse Spark 1.1 on July 9 with two structural firsts not present in any prior coverage — Meta is charging for model access for the first time ($1.25/$4.25 per million tokens) and has opened a public preview of the Meta Model API, letting outside developers call the Muse architecture directly. With leading tool-use benchmark scores (88.1 MCP Atlas, 54.7 JobBench), Meta becomes a fourth aggressive seller in the same agentic-workload segment that yesterday's Grok 4.5 and today's GPT-5.6 shipped into, priced below every competing flagship tier.

items.headline: Microsoft puts its 100-agent MDASH vulnerability-scanning harness into Windows-scale production
items.diff_narrative: New today: Microsoft announced on July 9 that MDASH, its multi-model agentic scanning harness orchestrating over 100 specialized AI agents, is moving onto dedicated cloud infrastructure for Windows-scale scanning, having already surfaced 16 vulnerabilities including four critical remote-code-execution flaws in the kernel TCP/IP stack and IKEv2 service. This is the defensive mirror of yesterday's JADEPUFFER story, in which an autonomous agent ran a ransomware intrusion end-to-end: within two news cycles, agentic vulnerability discovery has appeared on both the attacker and OS-vendor sides, and Microsoft is now arguing calendar-bound patch cycles must give way to continuous risk-driven remediation.

items.headline: AI events calendar: ICML's final workshop day lands tomorrow, Hot Chips early rate three weeks out
items.diff_narrative: Updated from yesterday's calendar: ICML Seoul has advanced from workshops running through the weekend to a last-call framing — July 11 is now the final day to catch sessions on-site or remote. The Hot Chips July 31 early-registration deadline is now flagged as three weeks out, and the recommended near-term actions have shifted to booking the August AI Risk Summit and Black Hat/DEF CON dates specifically because this week's GPT-5.6, Grok 4.5, and Muse Spark launches make the August-September circuit the likely venue for the first hands-on agentic-deployment retrospectives. The rest of the fall lineup (AI Infra Summit, The AI Conference, Ai4, GitHub Universe, re:Invent) carries over unchanged.
